hindi: माना कि $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है, $f(1)=1$, जिसके लिए सभी $x>0$ हेतु $x^{2}f'(x)=3xf(x)-\left(f(x)\right)^{2}$ है। माना कि $g:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है, $g(1)=0$, जिसके लिए सभी $x>0$ हेतु
solution_full: Divide the first equation by $x^{2}$: $f'(x)=3\dfrac{f}{x}-\left(\dfrac fx\right)^{2}$. The right side depends only on $\dfrac fx$, so the equation is homogeneous.
Put $f=vx$, $f'=v+xv'$: $v+xv'=3v-v^{2}$, so $x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=v(2-v)$. With $f(1)=1$, $v(1)=1$, and $v$ stays in $(0,2)$ (the constant solutions $v=0$ and $v=2$ cannot be crossed).
Separate the variables: $\dfrac{dv}{v(2-v)}=\dfrac{dx}{x}$. Partial fractions: $\dfrac{1}{v(2-v)}=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac1v+\dfrac1{2-v}\right)$, so $\dfrac12\ln\dfrac{v}{2-v}=\ln x+c$.
At $x=1$, $v=1$: $c=0$. Hence $\dfrac{v}{2-v}=x^{2}$, $v=\dfrac{2x^{2}}{1+x^{2}}$ and $f(x)=\dfrac{2x^{3}}{1+x^{2}}$, which is positive on $(0,\infty)$.
The second equation is linear in $g$ with $P(x)=\dfrac{2x}{1+x^{2}}$. Integrating factor: $e^{\ln(1+x^{2})}=1+x^{2}$.
originality_note: New: the integrating factor 1 + x^2 of the linear equation for g is exactly the denominator of f, which comes from the homogeneous equation, so (1 + x^2) f = 2x^3 and g becomes a polynomial (way 5). Closest known: 3x^2 dy = (3xy + y^2)dx type homogeneous exercises. Different because: the logistic-type v-equation and the cancellation with the second equation are new; web search found only different homogeneous equations.
blueprint_concepts: Linear differential equation in y; integrating factor

concept_use.Variable separable equations: After f = vx the homogeneous equation becomes x v' = v(2 - v), which is separated and integrated with partial fractions.
concept_use.Homogeneous differential equations: The equation for f has right side 3(f/x) - (f/x)^2, a function of f/x only, so the substitution f = vx is used.
concept_use.Linear differential equation in y; integ: The equation for g is linear with integrating factor 1 + x^2, and this factor cancels the denominator of f.
